name: Garlic
perishability: Semi-perishable. Cured bulbs keep 6–8 months in airy stores.
summary: A single-harvest, storable crop concentrated in the Malwa plateau of Madhya Pradesh and neighbouring Rajasthan. Because farmers decide area from last year's price, garlic swings through long boom–bust cycles: a 2022 crash to a few rupees a kilo was followed by retail prices of ₹400–500/kg in early 2024.

key_numbers.label: World rank
key_numbers.note: after China, which grows about three-quarters of world garlic

global: India is the second-largest garlic producer after China. It exports modest volumes (Bangladesh, Malaysia, Nepal, Vietnam, the Gulf) and has restricted Chinese garlic imports since 2014 on phytosanitary grounds; smuggled Chinese garlic still turns up when Indian prices spike.

rows.hubs: Mandsaur, Neemuch, Ratlam, Ujjain, Shajapur, Rajgarh, Guna
Punjab, Assam, Maharashtra, Haryana, Himachal, J&K, Tamil Nadu (Nilgiris, Kodaikanal)

belts.name: Mandsaur–Neemuch
belts.note: The national garlic hub; Mandsaur and Neemuch APMCs set prices for the country.

belts.name: Saurashtra
belts.note: Garlic for fresh trade and dehydration.

belts.name: Nilgiris and Kodaikanal hills
belts.note: Hill garlic with large, pungent bulbs (Kodaikanal Malai Poondu is GI tagged).

seasons.name: Rabi (plains)
seasons.note: Planted from cloves after the monsoon; harvested and cured in spring, then stored.

lean_season: October–January, as last season's stored garlic runs down before the new crop.

climate.v: Cool weather (12–18 °C) for leaf growth, then warmer days (20–25 °C) and longer daylight for bulbing.
Tolerates light frost; needs a cool spell for proper bulb formation.
Dry weather at maturity and curing. Rain at harvest causes rot and discoloured bulbs.
Well-drained loam, pH 6–7; heavy clay deforms bulbs.

weather_risks.risk: Unseasonal rain and hail at harvest
weather_risks.impact: Wet bulbs cure badly and rot in storage; lowers quality grade.
Poor bulb development and split cloves.
Delays planting and shortens the season.

pests.name: Thrips
pests.impact: Main pest; silvering of leaves and smaller bulbs.

pests.name: Eriophyid mite
pests.impact: Twisted leaves; carried in seed cloves and stores.

pests.name: Basal rot and white rot
pests.impact: Bulb rot in field and storage.

pests.name: Storage sprouting and weight loss
pests.impact: Weight loss of 15–25% over long storage.

postharvest.storage: Ambient ventilated stores (bundles hung or in mesh bags), or 0–2 °C at 65–70% RH.

loss.detail: Not reported separately; storage shrinkage of 15–25% is common.

practices: Cured in the field and in shade for 2–3 weeks with leaves on.
Graded by bulb size and clove count; large-bulb ('Ooty', 'Himachali', G-282) types fetch premiums.
Dehydration (flakes, powder) and peeled-garlic units absorb gluts.
Traded in 40–50 kg jute or mesh bags.

steps.what: Harvest, curing and bundling; many farmers store and sell through the year.
Mandsaur, Neemuch, Ratlam, Kota: open auction of trolley loads.
Store in town godowns and release through the year.
Loose and peeled garlic retail; paste, powder and flakes makers.

supply_chain.farmer_share: Not estimated in the RBI series.

varieties.name: G-282 (Yamuna Safed-3), G-1, Yamuna Safed (G-41)
varieties.note: NHRDF varieties; G-282 has large bulbs.

varieties.name: Desi (small clove, Malwa)
varieties.note: Pungent, stores well; the bulk of trade.

trade.exports: Modest: Bangladesh, Malaysia, Nepal, Vietnam, UAE; also dehydrated garlic.
trade.imports: Chinese garlic restricted since 2014; Afghan garlic enters occasionally.

policy.what: Imports of Chinese garlic restricted on phytosanitary grounds.
Madhya Pradesh Bhavantar (price-deficit) payments covered garlic in some seasons.
Seizures of smuggled Chinese garlic during the price spike.

history.what: Glut; farm prices fell to ₹5–10/kg in Malwa.
Farm prices of ₹1–5/kg; farmers dumped garlic and cut planting.
Smaller crop after the crash; retail ₹400–500/kg.
Area rebounded after the 2024 spike and prices fell back sharply.

signals: Arrivals and modal price at Mandsaur and Neemuch.
Planted area reports from MP and Rajasthan in Oct–Nov (area follows last year's price).
Rain during Feb–Apr harvest and curing.
Stock levels with traders in Aug–Nov.
business: Garlic is a cycle trade: high prices bring bigger plantings and a crash 12–18 months later. Track planted area, not just today's price.
Peeled garlic and paste carry large value-add on quick commerce (₹640/kg peeled vs ₹445/kg whole on Blinkit Delhi).
Storage works: cured garlic keeps for months, so buying at harvest in a weak year is the classic play.
